questions.title: What exactly is the difference between OSC’s investigative authority under §1216 versus the court‑initiated enforcement process under FOIA §552(a)(4)(F)(i), and why doesn’t §1216 automatically trigger an OSC investigation?
questions.question_body: I’m confused about why the court held that OSC’s failure to investigate DOJ under §1216 didn’t automatically give AFL standing. My understanding was that §1216(a)(3) says OSC “shall … conduct an investigation” of arbitrary FOIA withholdings. Yet the district court said OSC could decline because the three predicates in §552(a)(4)(F)(i) weren’t met. Exactly which statutory provisions are meant to limit OSC’s power, and how did the court reconcile that with the language in §1216?

questions.title: Which procedural doctrine governs the requirement for OSC to provide notices under §1214, and does that requirement apply when OSC is proceeding under §1216?
questions.question_body: The opinion repeatedly mentions that OSC’s decision to follow the notice and procedure rules of §1214 in a §1216 investigation is discretionary. How does the Supreme Court’s treatment of OSC’s procedural rights in cases like Carson v. U.S. Off. of Special Couns. affect whether a plaintiff can rely on those notice obligations to establish injury for standing?

questions.title: Why does the court treat a plaintiff’s informational injury as speculative when it arises from a third‑party agency’s failed FOIA production?
questions.question_body: AFL argues that OSC’s refusal to investigate DOJ has caused an ‘informational injury’ by preventing it from receiving detaine; the court says the injury is too speculative because it relies on DOJ’s future decision. What standard does the court apply to determine whether such an injury is concrete, and how does that differ from the conventional injury analysis used in §2(l)(A) cases?

questions.title: Can a statutory ‘procedural right’ that only exists in law and not in court (a right in vacuo) confer Article III standing even if it is not tied to a concrete, particularized injury?
questions.question_body: The opinion cites Summers v. Earth Island Inst. and Citizens for Const. Integrity v. Census Bureau, arguing that a procedural right in vacuo is insufficient for standing. Are there any cases where such a right did provide standing, and why does the court consider ‘procedure without an injury’ a dead end for Article III challenges?

questions.title: Does the relaxed standing standard for procedural injuries apply only to fully vested statutory entitlements, or can it extend to a ‘procedural right’ that is merely the absence of a proceeding?
questions.question_body: The court references Ctr. for Law & Educ. v. Dep’t of Educ. and Fla. Audubon Soc’y v. Bentsen for a relaxed standard. AFL tries to argue that OSC’s failure to investigate is a procedural injury under §1216. Does the relaxed standard apply in this context, or is there a line that distinguishes an actual procedural claim from a hypothetical one?

questions.title: What is the correct causal chain required for Article III standing when the alleged injury depends on a chain of separate agency actions?
questions.question_body: AFL’s first standing theory hinges on OSC→MSPB→DOJ producing records. The opinion says this chain is speculative. How do courts determine whether the chain is too attenuated to support standing, and are there examples where a multi‑step chain was deemed sufficient?

questions.title: Why does the court hold that redressability is satisfied only if a judgment binds the parties directly, not if it merely persuades third parties?
questions.question_body: The opinion cites Haaland v. Brackeen and FDA v. All. for Hippocratic Med., arguing that redressability must bind the parties, not just influence independent actors. Is there a clear doctrine or case law that explains why a court cannot order an agency to perform discretionary enforcement to prevent damage to a plaintiff?

questions.title: Is there any statutory entitlement to information under §1214 that could enable a plaintiff to claim a concrete injury when OSC conducts a §1216 investigation?
questions.question_body: The opinion says UFC’s lack of entitlement to notice under §1214 means there’s no concrete injury. What if §1216 investigation followed §1214 notice rules? Would that create a statutory right to those notices or information for a plaintiff, and is there precedent for a plaintiff’s entitlement to such procedural information under FOIA or MIS MP?
